new_value: Implemented (commit this round): per-source admission cap for the DTN buffer. lichen_router_dtn_buffer takes the storing source IID, counts valid records from that source, and rejects -ENOBUFS when CONFIG_LICHEN_ROUTER_DTN_MAX_PER_SOURCE (Kconfig default 2) is reached — applied BEFORE any eviction so a flooder cannot churn other sources' records. route_packet passes the packet's wire source IID; the record stores it for future authenticated-keying. routing_dispatch: MAX_PER_SOURCE=3 + case 17 (three stores OK, fourth -ENOBUFS, different source admitted). VALIDATED: routing_dispatch green (gcc-14, ASan/UBSan, -Werror). Reviews: 3 passes on kimi-k3 — pass 1 PASS (logic + accounting), pass 3 PASS (NULL-source legacy path consistent; dtn.c legacy API unaffected; bounded scan) with the router.h #ifndef fallback gap (fixed); pass 2 verified the anti-churn property and flagged the KEY GAP: the cap is keyed on the claimed wire source IID, not the LLSec-authenticated peer identity — IID rotation defeats it. Disposition: reduced threat model documented on router.h (cap bounds honest senders; rotation-resistant keying requires threading the authenticated sender IID through struct lichen_route_packet) and a follow-up bead filed for the authenticated keying. This lands the availability mitigation the bead asked for with the honest limit documented.
